parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, no documented anti-trans policing or violence, working courts and capital tolerance; against that, state-orchestrated demonisation, constitutional erasure of markers, and detention conditions flagged as unremedied. Hostility plus functioning institutions is partially liability, not recourse.

State-imposed universal exposures: sex-at-birth passports, border refusal/lifetime-ineligibility instructions, facility bans reaching most states (criminal in four, one arrest, men's-ward hold), documented custody abuse. Protective states and court stays exist but cannot offset the federal ceiling.

Documented airport ID stop, railway-police groping 'gender checks' and degrading custody; new penal code stripped trans-specific sexual-violence offences; high societal violence without trans disaggregation. Offsetting: constitutional equality rulings and operating high-court guidelines.

No border friction, foreign X markers accepted, facilities and anti-discrimination protected, 91% public acceptance. Deductions: custody placement unregulated by birth-sex records with documented assaults, and few convictions despite rising reports. Protective core outweighs a contingent detention gap.

Article 521 criminalises trans feminine presentation (six years) with documented enforcement; 534 in force, police arrests and prosecutor-ordered anal exams, pride cancelled by security forces, rising violence. Judicial softening and occasional marker change are not remedy for a visitor.
